Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

sudden adjective

also unexpected, abrupt, a sudden storm, sudden death

classical

Cic. Tusc. 3.52: maris subita tempestās (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 1.23.7: ista subita … benignitās

subitus, subita, subitum

adjective, declension

sudden, unexpected

The everyday word: what comes on all at once, a storm, a death, a fright. Lewis & Short also gives it for soldiers raised in haste (Tac. H. 4.76) and, of a slope, steep (Stat.); as a noun, subitum is something that has suddenly come up, an urgent matter (subitum est ei remigrāre, Cic. Fam. 13.2). The adverb is subitō (see suddenly).

Other words

  • repentīnus, repentīna, repentīnum — sudden, unlooked for

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.13.4: repentīna fit quiēs; Cic. Off. 1.27: repentīnō aliquō mōtū

    Sudden as against expected or prepared: Cicero sets it against exspectātus and against meditātus et praeparātus (Lewis & Short). Of people it means upstart (ignōtī hominēs et repentīnī, Cic. Brut. 242, Lewis & Short).

  • imprōvīsus, imprōvīsa, imprōvīsum — unforeseen, unexpected

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Agr. 2.60: amor tam imprōvīsus ac tam repentīnus

    Not foreseen, the point being that no one saw it coming. Its ablative makes an adverb: dē imprōvīsō, suddenly, without warning.

Examples

  • silentium et repentīna fit quiēs

    silence falls, and a sudden calmLiv. 1.13.4

  • namque ista subita mē jubet benignitās vigilāre, faciās nē meā culpā lucrum

    for this sudden kindness of yours tells me to stay awake, so that you make no profit through my faultPhaedr. 1.23.7–8

  • Unde iste amor tam imprōvīsus ac tam repentīnus?

    Where does this love of his come from, so unforeseen and so sudden?Cic. Agr. 2.60

  • Leviōra enim sunt ea, quae repentīnō aliquō mōtū accidunt, quam ea, quae meditāta et praeparāta īnferuntur.

    For wrongs done on some sudden impulse are lighter than those that are thought out and prepared.Cic. Off. 1.27

See also suddenly, surprise.
